derivative.def: The instantaneous rate of change of a function. At $x = a$, $f'(a) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$ when the limit exists; found at every $x$, it is the derivative function $f'(x)$.

tangent-line.def: The line through $(a, f(a))$ whose slope is $f'(a)$: $y = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)$. It is the limit of secant lines through that point.

leibniz.def: Writing the derivative of $y = f(x)$ as $\frac{dy}{dx}$, and "the derivative of" as $\frac{d}{dx}$. Its value at $x = a$ is written $\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=a}$.
